text:
Dmitri: Quick heads-up — we saw a regression on the FP8 rollout for Mistral-7B-Inst when under mixed-length workloads. tail latency up ~18% on p95 after the kernel switch.
Anya: Ugh. Is this the FP8 kernel itself or something in the routing/batching layer?
Dmitri: Early profiling points to two things: (1) kernel selection is falling back to a slower matmul path for sequences >1024 because the estimator is using avg_seq_len instead of p95, and (2) KV cache layout change introduced an extra copy when we serve short-turn dialogs.
Max: Do you have a flamegraph or perf profile?
Dmitri: Uploaded to the perf bucket: https://redwood.internal/perf/mistral/fp8/180345 — main hotspots around `matmul_fp8_generic` and `kv_cache_relayout`.
Rachel: The avg vs p95 thing sounds familiar — we tuned batching heuristic for throughput so it picks kernels that are great for avg, not tails. We should add a tail-weighted metric.
Anya: For KV copy, is that from alignment to 16B boundaries for FP8 packing?
Dmitri: Yep. We changed the on-device layout to pack bytes for FP8 which reduced overall memory but the relayout in the runtime executes a memcpy for every decode step on short sequences. That kills latency.
Ciara: Possible quick mitigation: only enable relayout for batches with total tokens > threshold, otherwise use legacy layout. We can gate that in kernel selection policy.
Max: I can throw a quick patch to runtime: if (batch_tokens < 8k) skip relayout. Want me to PR?
Dmitri: Please. Also we need to adjust kernel selector to consider p95_seq_len. Current selector config: `seq_metric: avg, pref: throughput`. Change to `seq_metric: p95, perf_target: latency` for the Mistral FP8 profile.
Rachel: Agree. But watch out — switching to p95 will reduce throughput for stable long-running workloads. We should make it model-profile specific.
Anya: That's the point — model-specific quant profiles should carry the selector policy. We have three fields: quant_type, kernel_preferences, seq_metric. Add them to the profile artifact.
Ciara: Where do we store the profiles? There's the models repo and the quant-profiles S3 bucket. Which canonical?
Dmitri: Let's standardize: publish a small JSON artifact under the model entry in the model-registry: `/models/mistral-7b/profiles/quant_fp8_runtime.json` and a signed copy in S3 for runtime retrieval.
Max: Example profile snippet I propose:
```json
{
  "quant_type": "fp8",
  "kernel_prefs": ["fast_fp8_matmul", "fallback_int8_matmul"],
  "seq_metric": "p95",
  "kv_layout": "packed_fp8_conditional",
  "relayout_threshold_tokens": 8192
}
```
Rachel: Looks good. Also add `compat_models` list to say which model hashes were calibrated with this profile.
Dmitri: Calibration note — we saw slight perplexity drift when we used the short calibration set. For Mistral we need a 5k sample calibration drawn from multi-turn dialogs, not single-turn. That explains BLEU-like quality drop for some prompts.
Anya: Can you add the calibration commit ID and dataset name to the artifact? `calib_commit` and `calib_dataset` fields.
Dmitri: Will do. Also PerfBot please run regression check after the PR merges.
PerfBot: @Dmitri regression job queued: `perf/checks/mistral-fp8/180345`. Will report p50/p95/p99 and throughput delta in ~30m. :robot_face:
Ciara: One more thing — INT8 fallback is faster on A100 for long sequences in our current kernels. We should include guidance in the profile: prefer INT8 on A100 when seq_metric = p99.
Max: Good call. I can add hardware hints: `prefer_on: {"A100": "int8", "H100": "fp8"}`
Rachel: After Max's runtime patch and profile update, let's run A/B on dedicated clusters and host to ensure no SLA impact. Also add a canary with 5% traffic.
Anya: I'll add a short doc in the model-registry README describing creation and vetting of quant profiles and where to share configs.
Dmitri: PRs: runtime patch (#4472), profile artifact (#4473). Linking both in the perf ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INF-1623
Ciara: Thanks — this plan should get us back to prior p95 and keep the benefits of FP8 overall.
Max: PR incoming in ~45m.
PerfBot: Regression check complete: p95 delta -3% (improved), throughput -1.2% on canary. Full report: https://redwood.internal/perf/reports/180345.
Dmitri: Nice. Keep an eye on quality regressions from calibration. We'll re-run evals on the full prompt-set overnight.
Rachel: Great coordination — let's sync in the standup tomorrow if anything flaps.
